'''Sube Shrine''' (すべじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Hamana-ku, Hamamatsu|Q117077169|qid=Q117077169}}, {{ill|Hamamatsu|Q185125|qid=Q185125}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It is an {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki shrine}}, one of six shrines of {{ill|Inasa District, Shizuoka|Q11487138|qid=Q11487138}} in {{ill|Tōtōmi Province|Q1048864|qid=Q1048864}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, its former rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== Overview ===
According to shrine tradition, it was founded in {{ill|Ninna|Q1346317|qid=Q1346317}} 3 (887), during the reign of the 58th emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōkō|Q440518|qid=Q440518}}. Its location, {{ill|Miyakodacho|Q131901548|qid=Q131901548}}, developed as a {{ill|mikuriya|Q11488831|qid=Q11488831}} of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}, and the deities are thought to have been invited from Ise. Originally, the Inner Shrine stood as upper shrine on Uenoyama in Kami-Miyakoda Sube, and the Outer Shrine stood as lower shrine in Nakatsu of Shimo-Miyakoda. In {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} 2 (902), both were moved to the present site and came to be called {{ill|Shinmei shrines|Q11590310|qid=Q11590310|lt=Shinmei-gū}} or Sube Shrine.

=== Enshrined deities ===
*Inner Shrine main sanctuary ({{ill|chigi and katsuogi|Q87220234|qid=Q87220234|lt=chigi}} inward-cut, {{ill|chigi and katsuogi|Q87220234|qid=Q87220234|lt=katsuogi}} six)
**{{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100|lt=Main deity}}: {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu-Ōmikami}}
**{{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100|lt=Associated deities}}: {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|Q849412|qid=Q849412|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Takuhadachiji-hime|Q11110848|qid=Q11110848|lt=Takuhatachijihime-no-Mikoto}}
*Outer Shrine main sanctuary (chigi outward-cut, katsuogi five)
**Enshrined deity: {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Q2983724|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke Ōkami}}
**Associated deities: {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Q1056017|qid=Q1056017|lt=Imperial grandson Ninigi-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Futodama|Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|lt=Ame-no-Futodama-no-Mikoto}}
*Outer shrine: 69 village shrines of Miyakoda village {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}}
*Precinct shrines
** Akiba Shrine: {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|Q1640658|qid=Q1640658|lt=Hi-no-Kagutsuchi-no-Kami}}
** Tsushima Shrine / Ubagami Shrine: {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Takehayasusanoo-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|Q6080112|qid=Q6080112|lt=Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto}}

=== Festivals ===
At the autumn {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=annual grand festival}}, floats from nine surrounding districts (Kawayama, Araki, Yokoo, Yoshikage, Tanigami, Isshiki, Nakatsu, Nakano, Sube) are pulled around. Also, at the {{ill|Kinensai|Q118906710|qid=Q118906710}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}}, children selected from duty districts and ujiko participate by serving offering rites and dedicating {{ill|Urayasu no mai|ja|浦安の舞|qid=Q11558194}} (sword dance and bell dance).
